data.description:
Operator directive 2026-08-12 (overrides DESIGN.md's 'no dark mode by Wednesday' ruling — deliberately; ~22h runway acknowledged; aesthetic nice-touch, must not disturb the live fleet: all work in a linked worktree).

WHAT: A multi-theme system for Marquee. Day (current Flight Deck) stays the default and is untouched. Themes are palette-token overrides under html[data-theme=...] — structure tokens (spacing, radius, hairline, type, shadow:none) are theme-invariant in every theme. Adding a theme = one CSS block + one row in a small THEMES registry that the switcher renders. Persistence via localStorage; no prefers-color-scheme auto-switch (Day unless explicitly chosen).

PHASE 1 — PROTOTYPE (the design gate, binding): in prototypes/pipeline-v1.1/index.html, build the theme machinery + a fixed-width instrument-style theme switch in the top bar (elements never jump), and FOUR themes beyond Day:
  1. Three distinct NIGHT candidates, each resting on a different aesthetic bet (e.g. blue-black re-lit instrument w/ luminous accent; amber/red-shift cockpit night-vision; neutral graphite). Operator picks ONE — the others are deleted before the app fold.
  2. VAPORWAVE — a fun theme proving arbitrary-theme extensibility; palette-only vaporwave (deep indigo/magenta/cyan) still obeying every Flight Deck craft rule.
All palettes contrast-measured like Day (ratios in comments; nothing under 4.5:1 for text). The 8 track colors get per-theme octaves where needed. Agenda canvas relationship re-tuned per theme. ~85 raw hex outside :root in the prototype get tokenized as encountered.

PHASE 2 — APP (after operator picks the night winner): lift machinery + Day/Night/Vaporwave into src/styles/tokens.css + switcher; tokenize the ~36 raw hex in src and 8 in components.css; extend check:design with a no-raw-hex-outside-tokens.css rule (small allowlist) so themes cannot rot.

Branch/worktree: mrq-themes via Marquee-worktrees. Do not merge near the submission window without operator go-ahead.
data.title: Theme system: Day default plus selectable themes — three night-mode candidates and Vaporwave in the prototype, winner + machinery to the app

provenance.reason: Plan is in the ticket description; design work proceeding in worktree

data.body: Prototype phase built and committed on mrq-103-themes (5603668). Vaporwave REMOVED by operator ruling 2026-08-12 — scope is now Day + one night winner from three candidates; the registry machinery still supports arbitrary themes. Day is unchanged and default; ~90 hardcoded colors tokenized; all palettes contrast-measured >=4.5:1; 22 routes x 4 themes verified in-browser with zero JS errors. Awaiting operator pick: N1 Midnight Ops / N2 Red-Shift / N3 Graphite.

Complete through the app fold. Night = Graphite (operator pick 2026-08-12); Midnight Ops and Red-Shift deleted, Vaporwave deleted earlier.

Shipped on mrq-103-themes (5 commits, tip ae9af8a):
- Prototype v1.11: Day + Night, ~90 colors tokenized, ?theme= override for comparison links.
- App: tokens.css night block; theme.ts registry; pre-paint stamp in index.html (no flash); Topbar select; components.css now has ZERO literal colors.
- DESIGN.md: no-dark-mode ruling replaced with a Themes section carrying the binding rules.
- check:design gains two rules, each verified failing on a real violation first: no literal colors in components.css; night must redefine every color token Day introduces.
- 9 theme tests in the Worker-free pool, 238ms, verified failing on a seeded regression.

Scope decisions worth keeping: track colors are NOT rewritten at night (organizer data, painted as borders/dots, no contrast duty); public agenda/embeds/API docs keep their own palettes (an embed inherits its host page).

Gate: 3x tsc, vite build, check:design, check:api, trace:ac, theme tests — all green. Real-artifact check: local Worker on :8799 serves the night block and the pre-paint script from the built bundle. NOT merged — deadline window; awaiting operator.

Validation on the rebased tree (github/main c94351e -> merged 9eaa9bf): three tsc projects clean, vite build green, check:design pass (including the two new theme rules), check:api pass, trace:ac pass, 9 theme tests pass in 136ms. Both new check:design rules and the 9 tests were each verified FAILING on a seeded real violation before being kept. Real-artifact check: local Worker on :8799 served the night block and the pre-paint script from the built bundle, and the built CSS carries [data-theme=night]. Full npm test deliberately skipped: load average 35 on 16 cores, the documented false-red condition; ran the standing contention gate instead.

Merged via PR #60 (squash) to main as 9eaa9bf, after a rebase onto c94351e that resolved three conflicts against another agent's cold-start work — its v1.11 prototype label kept, the theme prototype deferred to v1.12. Verified post-merge on github/main: night block in tokens.css, theme.ts present, prototype at v1.12.

data.body:
Board reconciliation 2026-08-12: status left as DONE, deliberately, and NOT touched — a separate Theme Rescue agent (workspace:13 surface:566) owns this ground right now and reconciliation must not race it.

For the record, done is correct for what this ticket scoped: PR #60 (mrq-103-themes, 'theme system — Day default, Night opt-in') merged 2026-08-12T06:01:03Z and is an ancestor of github/main; src/ui/shell/theme.ts is present on main.

What is NOT on main is the follow-on work on branch theme-round. That branch IS now pushed (github/theme-round @ ea3041d7) — the earlier report that it was never pushed is out of date, presumably because the rescue agent pushed it. It carries 13 commits main does not have (register theme classes, three register palettes, Topbar/Sidebar register chrome, dashboard variants, registry unit tests, palette relabel to Marquee Light / Marquee Night, plus browser proof shots), and it is 61 commits BEHIND github/main, so it needs a merge-forward before it can land. That work has no ticket of its own. I am not minting one — ticket creation is single-writer and belongs to the orchestrator. Flagging it here and in the reconciliation summary so it does not fall through the floor.

Theme round two (register themes) rescued and put on the remote — the work was NEVER pushed, and every agent that built it was dead on a quota error.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY THERE. This ticket's original scope (Day/Night palette system) did merge, as PR #60 -> 9eaa9bf, so "done" was correct for that. What was stranded on the local-only branch `theme-round` was a SECOND round: three *register* themes (latent.space, AI Engineer, swyxy) that swap nav labels, search glyph and dashboard renderers, not just palette. ~12 commits, never on any remote.

PUSHED FIRST. Branch pushed before reading a line of the diff, and archived intact at `theme-round-archive` before any history rewriting.

REBASED. main had moved 61 commits. Rebuilt as `theme-registers` off current main. Two real conflicts, both resolved toward main's newer structure: Sidebar.tsx (main's Organization nav group, EventSwitcher, eventScopedPath/slug threading all kept, register chrome layered on top) and DashboardPage.tsx (main's SetupChecklistCard + InstancePanel kept).

SCOPE NARROWED. The branch also carried a .lattice board snapshot and sequence/research/cli-parity.md (MRQ-104 research). Both excluded. The board snapshot mattered most: it was a stale copy reading in_progress for this ticket while the live board has it done, and merging it would have fought the primary checkout's live uncommitted board state. Both remain on theme-round-archive for whoever owns MRQ-104.

A CONTRACT TEST EARNED ITS KEEP. An uncommitted test on the branch pinned swyxy's nav overrides to the route table. On rebase it failed immediately: main had added nine sidebar routes the register knew nothing about (people, lists, sourcing, submissions, submission-new, speakers, files, tasks, embeds). Without it, swyxy would have silently reverted those nine to title-case mid-nav.

REVIEWED BY SOMEONE ELSE. An independent review agent returned approve-with-nits and found two real defects: (1) `?theme=day` desynced the document from the app — the pre-paint id map had no "day" key, so the override fell through to storage; (2) swyxy's dark/light toggle was inert under `?mode=` because the observer re-read the URL. Both fixed, both verified in a browser, three regression tests added.

VALIDATED IN A REAL BROWSER, not just green tests. Built Worker, local D1 with the full 9,980-row seed, driven through the c11 embedded browser with `--var INSECURE_LOCAL_COOKIES:1` (without it the browser 401s after a 200 login, and curl never sees it). All five themes render the live dashboard with real data. Elements-never-jump measured: the select holds 118px and the identity block sits at x=1354 in every theme, and swyxy's dark<->light toggle leaves the button, the select and the identity block pixel-identical.

GATE. `npm run pr-gate` pass at 104s/120s. The unit suite reported pass-over-budget at 96s vs its 45s budget under load 5.45/10.11/11.80 with 32 users; the same code ran 63s under lighter load, and this PR's three added tests take 12ms — that is contention, not the diff.

PR #114 open, awaiting re-review of the fix commit before merge. Merging does not deploy; the deploy owner will be told separately.

OPEN OPERATOR QUESTION (c11 flag raised): swyxy wanted `--radius: 6px`; DESIGN.md holds radius theme-invariant. I honored DESIGN.md and dropped it rather than amending the doc.

MERGED. PR #114 squash-merged to main as 06385e08 (single parent, one commit — a revert is one command if it ever needs rolling back).

The register round is now on the remote and on main. Final state:

- Five themes ship: Marquee Light (default, no attribute), Marquee Night, latent.space, AI Engineer, swyxy.
- Two review rounds by an independent agent. Round one: approve-with-nits, four blockers. Round two: merge, after verifying every fix and finding that the structure-token test I had added guarded only the first of 59 scoped blocks — tightened, and the tightening proven by injecting `--radius: 6px` into swyxy's dark-mode block (the 25th) and watching the new test fail where the old one passed.
- Gate green at 104s/120s on the merged tree.
- Browser-validated on the built Worker with the full 9,980-row seed.

Naming note for the record: the topbar reads "Marquee Light" / "Marquee Night", per the operator's own commit ea3041d7 at 14:25 today, which explicitly superseded the earlier "Marquee Day" / "Marquis Night" wordplay. Nothing was renamed by this rescue.

MERGING DOES NOT DEPLOY (DEPLOY.md). The deploy owner has been told the change is on main.

Follow-ups left open, none blocking:
- check:design does not glob src/styles/themes/*.css, so register stylesheets are ungoverned by the no-raw-hex rule. Deliberately deferred rather than adding a new check hours before a deadline; worth a ticket, because the next register author walks straight into the gap.
- A few alpha-variant literals remain in latent-space.css and ai-engineer.css. They cannot be derived from a hex token without color-mix() or RGB-triplet tokens.
- DESIGN.md scopes registers to "the shell plus the program home", but swyxy and latent.space lowercase some chrome on every route. Either the doc widens or the CSS narrows.

OPEN OPERATOR QUESTION (c11 flag still raised): swyxy wanted --radius: 6px; DESIGN.md holds radius theme-invariant. I honored DESIGN.md and dropped it rather than amending the doc, and did not re-apply 6px via selectors — that would satisfy the letter and break the spirit. If registers should be allowed to move radius, the doc and the new test both need the amendment.
